2.text: shot a Chukchee man falls down. The Chukchee would tear up a hummock, and dig out a place

3.text: under it. Then they would sit down and cover themselves with hummocks,¹ looking through the
3.note: Footnote marker keyed as superscript ¹ per §2.10; draft read it as bare 'i'.

4.text: long grass hanging around. Thus they killed them all, and they were more than twenty.

5.text: “Another party went across the tundra, and arrived at the hamlet Duvannoye, on the Kolyma

6.text: River. It was in the night-time. Numerous people lived there. The Chukchee killed them all.
6.note: A small ink speck sits between 'It' and 'was' on the raster; not a letter, keyed as nothing (§2.14).

7.text: Previously they had pierced with knives the bottoms of the boats lying on the shore, so that when

8.text: the people tried to flee to the river with these boats, the boats sank and the people were drowned.

9.text: From there the Chukchee went to the mouth of the Omolon River, but the Yukaghir of Omolon

10.text: drove them back. They tell that tale themselves. Many other Chukchee dispersed on the tundra.

11.text: The ancient Yukaghir used to put beads into their dead-falls for bait. They would string them on

12.text: a thread and hang them inside, and connect them with the trigger. The Chukchee would creep

13.text: in for these beads, and then be caught under the falling weight. The owner would come and see

14.text: the blockhead lying there still alive. Then the Chukchee would try to speak Russian: ‘Kotora
14.note: Draft misread 'lying' as 'Iving'; corrected against the raster. Quote opening the Russian phrase is single curly (inner speech nested inside the paragraph's double-quoted narration).

15.text: topora, shita, bita!’ The Russian would thereupon treat the guest to whatever he had in his hand,
15.note: Draft dropped the closing single curly quote after 'bita!'; confirmed at 4x.

16.text: were it axe or spear. So after a while all of them were exterminated.”
16.note: Closing curly double quote for the paragraph opened at line 5 ('"Another party...').

17.note: No space keyed before the colon per §2.9, though the plate shows a thin space.

18.text: “On the Anadyr side there were also numerous people, and the Chukchee exterminated all
18.note: Draft rendered the opening quote as a guillemet «; confirmed curly double “ at 2x.

19.text: of them. There was a town there. People lived in that town early in the fall. Then in the

20.text: evening ravens began to gather from all sides, croaking incessantly. The old men and the old

21.text: women would say, ‘Why are they croaking so? It seems as if the Chukchee wanted to attack us
21.note: Opening quote for the nested speech is single curly, not double as the draft has it.

22.text: again!’ Some gave credence, and others did not. Then the Chukchee really came at early dawn,
22.note: Closing quote for the nested speech opened at line 21 is single curly.

23.text: attacked them in their sleep, killed the men, and took the women captive. One woman had a

24.text: babe at the breast. She fled with that child in her arms. After a while she heard pursuers coming.

25.text: Looking back, she saw two men driving reindeer and following her. When she looked back, one

26.text: shot at her and hit the baby. So it was killed. The mother fell over the little one with a loud

27.text: wail. They caught her and carried her away. She had a knife, so she drew it forth and killed

28.text: herself. Three other women were led away by the Chukchee. On the way one escaped. There

29.text: was a steep, overhanging river-bank partly fallen down. She crept into the hollow, and they could

30.text: not find her. They thrust their spears into the hollow, pierced her coat in several places, but were

31.text: unable to hit her body. They spent a whole day there, and at last went away. Two other women

32.text: were carried away. Their husbands were absent. Both were rich. When they came back and

33.text: found no wives, they began to prepare something by way of ransom. They bought tobacco.

34.text: Those Chukchee lived on an island across the strait. The two husbands went in a boat to that

35.text: island. One woman, seeing her husband, began to cry. The other was quite insensible. At the

36.text: same time both had nursing infants in their arms. The men offered ransom, — a bagful of

37.text: tobacco for each head. The Chukchee said, ‘We will give back the women, but the children we
37.note: Opening quote for the nested speech is single curly, not double as the draft has it.

38.text: will not give back.’ So they put the women into the boat and rowed away. The Chukchee
38.note: Closing quote for the nested speech opened at line 37 is single curly, confirmed at 4x.

39.text: husbands stood on the shore with the babes in their arms. As soon as the women left, one of

40.text: the Chukchee wailed aloud and slapped himself on his thighs with open palms. ‘Oh, but I am a
40.note: Opening quote for the nested speech is single curly, confirmed at 4x.

41.text: fool! I took the tobacco and lost the woman! Where shall I find another one like her!’ The
41.note: Closing quote for the nested speech opened at line 40 is single curly, confirmed at 4x.

42.text: other was silent, as if insensible; and lo, the other woman three times fled back to the Chukchee.

43.text: Twice she was rescued betimes; the third time she was lost altogether. Doubtless the Chukchee

44.text: altered her soul by means of shamanistic magic.”
44.note: Closing curly double quote for the paragraph opened at line 18 ('"On the Anadyr side...').

45.text: It is not easy to distinguish in these stories the element of fiction from

46.text: possible historical events. The watch-tower in the Chukochya hamlet really

47.text: existed. When visiting the place, I have seen its ruins on the ground. The

48.text: watch was probably directed against the western people living on the Big

49.text: Chukchee River. We find thereabouts a number of geographical names
